cases.description: All mandatory obligations are positively supported, applicable, authorized, temporally known and verified.
Positive and negative admissible evidence coexist for one mandatory semantic obligation.
A mandatory payload-integrity obligation has no evidence and has not been verified.
Required evidence was first received after the selected historical knowledge cutoff.
Dependency observer coverage is unknown, so the empty impact set cannot preserve the claim.
Verified counterevidence establishes that the evidence concerns a different physical subject.
The claim context is affirmatively outside the declared model applicability domain.
Payload evidence is present but the producer's authority cannot be established.
The named current trust policy explicitly denies the producer in a counterfactual replay.
An unverified advisory defeater hypothesis is retained but does not become an adverse finding or block the claim by itself.
A source event is definitely not yet effective at every possible physical acquisition instant; this is distinct from evidence being received late.
Event-effectivity and physical-acquisition time bounds overlap, so subject-time applicability is ambiguous.
The declared event or physical-acquisition time interval is malformed and cannot support an effectivity inference.
